function.name: math_power
function.description: Calculate the power of one number raised to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

mod.description: The modulus. Default is 1. Calculates pow(base, exponent) % mod when provided.

message.content:
I’m not entirely sure what you’re asking.  
Could you clarify whether you’d like me to compute:

1. \(3^{4}\) (i.e., 3 raised to the 4th power), or  
2. \((3^{4})^{\text{something}}\) (i.e., 3 raised to the 4th power, then that result raised to another exponent), or  
3. \(3^{(4^{\text{something}})}\) (i.e., 3 raised to the power of 4 raised to another exponent)?

Let me know which interpretation you intended, and I’ll do the calculation for you.
